problems: RANGES EVERYWHERE: Every single number is a range. 'Negative $8–15/bbl', '10–12 days', '70–80%', '₹40,000–50,000 crore', '₹2.5–3.5 lakh crore'. Ranges signal the analyst hasn't committed. CEO hears 'we don't know.' Pick the single most defensible number for each.
SITUATION IS 112 WORDS: Target is 2 sentences creating urgency. This is a paragraph. Cut by 60%.

JARGON — MULTIPLE VIOLATIONS: 'bbl', 'bpd', 'ESPO', 'Kozmino', 'Section 35A', 'ADNOC', 'Fujairah cargo loading slot', 'MoPNG', 'PSU refiners'. A non-oil CEO will lose the thread at 'Section 35A'. Each one costs 5+ seconds.

PERFORMANCE DATA HAS FOUR KPIs, EACH WITH RANGES: Maximum 3 numbers per field. The KPI block alone has 14+ numbers. It reads as a data dump, not a proof. Two of these KPIs (refining margin, April supply) are inputs to the crisis — they belong in situation, not a separate data block.

DECISION 2 IS A DECISION TREE, NOT A DECISION: 'If X do Y, if not do Z' means the CEO is being asked to pre-approve two contradictory actions. A decision asks for one commitment. Split into two decisions or collapse into the single most likely path with a named fallback.

DECISION 3 IS OPERATIONALLY DENSE: 'Two parallel calls', 'Fujairah cargo loading slot', 'Kozmino loading order', 'ESPO grace period' — this is a to-do list for a logistics manager, not a CEO ask. CEO needs to authorise MEA to act, not understand the supply chain.

ANALYSIS FINDING 2 BURIES THE LEAD: The so-what ('activate fuel depot rationing') is the most operationally urgent action on the page and it's hidden at the end of bullet 2. It should surface in decisions immediately.
CONDENSED PS HAS RANGES AND DOUBLE-COUNTS SITUATION: The PS repeats numbers from the situation field verbatim. It should add framing, not restate facts.
HEADER IS STRONG BUT PASSIVE ON TIMING: 'within days' is vague when the body says 3–5 days. Header should use the hardest number available.
'WASHINGTON CALL' IS UNDEFINED: Analysis finding 3 says 'a Washington call within 24 hours' without naming who calls whom about what. CEO cannot act on this without clarification.
fixes: HEADER REWRITE: 'Approve financial guarantees and crude reallocation by midnight April 2 — HPCL Mumbai shuts in 4 days and IOCL Bina cuts fuel to 200 million people by April 5.'

SITUATION REWRITE (2 sentences): 'One refinery has already shut; six more follow within 4 days because refiners are losing ₹500 crore daily and have no legal cover to keep operating. Maharashtra and Karnataka lose fuel first — then landlocked central India, triggering a humanitarian crisis the ₹45,000 crore backstop prevents.'

COLLAPSE PERFORMANCE DATA TO 3 NUMBERS, NO RANGES: (1) Refining margin: negative $12/bbl today vs. positive $5/bbl last quarter. (2) Crude runway at highest-risk sites: 11 days vs. government minimum of 15. (3) Guarantee required: ₹45,000 crore — less than 2% of GDP at stake.

REPLACE ALL JARGON: 'bpd' → 'barrels per day (a daily flow measure)' or cut entirely; 'ESPO/Kozmino' → 'Russian crude pipeline shipment'; 'Section 35A circular' → 'emergency RBI banking directive'; 'ADNOC Fujairah slot' → 'UAE emergency crude cargo'; 'MoPNG' → spell out on first use.

DECISION 2 REWRITE — ONE ASK: 'Confirm by April 2, 18:00 IST how much domestic ONGC crude can legally be redirected to Mumbai. If below 10,000 barrels/day, activate 15% fuel rationing across four states the same night. Owner: Petroleum Secretary.' Remove the conditional framing — brief the CEO on both paths verbally.

DECISION 3 REWRITE — ONE ASK: 'Authorise MEA to open simultaneous diplomatic calls within 24 hours to secure UAE emergency crude and a 60-day extension on Russian supply access, framed as a humanitarian food-and-fuel request. Require binary confirmation by April 4 midnight. Owner: MEA Secretary.'

NAME THE 'WASHINGTON CALL': Replace 'Washington call' with 'a direct call from the Foreign Secretary to the US Deputy Secretary of State requesting humanitarian flexibility on Russian crude sanctions enforcement' — or if that is not the right channel, name the correct one.

CONDENSED PS REWRITE: 'Six refineries shut in 4 days without action. The ₹45,000 crore guarantee required is less than 2% of the ₹3 lakh crore GDP loss if they do. Three decisions — issued simultaneously, tonight — prevent it.'
